title: Brass band, carnivals and returning in 1923
summary: Played D-flat in carnival brass bands; small country carnivals; four years in Hummel; back in 1923.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Oh, I was going to ask, did you ever play in a brass band with your clarinet, like an E flat clarinet or anything?

No, I never played no E flat, but I played D flat in the brass band that I got for carnivals when I played Scamina and yeah, I played three carnivals with Eleanor, I believe. Well, I, I was the one that had the job, so that made me up to get those. So you got your own band. Yeah, I got them all.
Did they have any carnival much up in the country at Tividow or those little towns? No, well, no, they never had no big carnival.

Well, yeah, they used to have a small couple of floats, you know. They'd have some greats up there too. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Because we always lucky enough to be playing on them nights, you know. Every, every, every holiday night we was playing somewhere.

Yeah, different places. And we played in Hummel over four years every Sunday night. Yeah, well, in fact, after I quit him, I came down here. Yeah. Well, he was, his son taking over the band, you know. And my brother was out there at that time. Mm-hmm. But I've been down here now over, well, since I, since 20, since, I came back the last time, but 1923, I think. Came back.
You went back to Tividow after the district closed. Yeah, I stayed a while. Then came back here again in 1923. Yeah. Yeah.
Because I didn't play very much after I went back out there, because my brother was playing.
